records.source: וַנֵּ֜פֶן וַנִּסַּ֤ע הַמִּדְבָּ֨רָה֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יַם־ס֔וּף כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וַנָּ֥סָב אֶת־הַר־שֵׂעִ֖יר יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And we turned and set out [toward] the wilderness [by the] way of [the] Sea of Reeds, as spoke Yahweh to me; and we went around the hill country of Seir many days.
pieces: So we turned back and headed into the wilderness by the Red Sea road, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me, and we spent a long time going around the hill country of Seir.

L.1: And we turned and set out into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to me; and we went around the hill country of Seir many days.

R.1: Then we turned around and went back into the desert on the road toward the Red Sea, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me. For a long time we kept going around the hill country of Seir.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had spoken to me: Israel now obeys the order of 1:40
decisions.reason: After the people refused to enter the land and were beaten at Hormah, God told them to turn and go back into the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Reeds (1:40). This verse uses the same words to say that this time they did as they were told.

decisions.choice: the way of the Sea of Reeds: the road south toward the gulf east of Sinai
decisions.reason: "Sea of Reeds" is the name of the sea of the crossing (Exodus 13:18; 15:4), and it is also used for the gulf at Elath and Ezion-geber (1 Kings 9:26; verse 8). Here it names the road leading south toward that gulf, as in Numbers 21:4.

decisions.choice: we went around the hill country of Seir many days: a long time spent moving about the region of Edom
decisions.reason: Seir is the mountain country of Edom, south-east of the Dead Sea (Genesis 36:8). "Many days" covers the long years in the wilderness; verse 14 counts thirty-eight years from Kadesh-barnea to the Zered. The verb pictures circling round, not a straight march.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:4: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

records.heading: Passing by Edom, Moab and Ammon

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, saying,
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me,

L.2: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, saying,

decisions.choice: no word for "saying"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew introduces the quotation with "saying", which English does not need after "said".

records.source: רַב־לָכֶ֕ם סֹ֖ב אֶת־הָהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה פְּנ֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם צָפֹֽנָה׃
records.gloss: Enough for you going around the hill country this; turn yourselves northward.
pieces: 'Your circling of this hill country has gone on long enough. Turn north now.

L.3: '[It is] enough for you, going around this hill country; turn northward.

R.3: 'That is enough going around these hills. Now head north.

decisions.choice: enough for you: it is time to stop and move on
decisions.reason: The same words opened God's command at Horeb, "You have stayed long enough at this mountain" (1:6). Each time they mark the end of one stage of the journey and the start of the next.

decisions.choice: northward: toward the lands east of the Dead Sea and the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel had been in the region south of Edom. Turning north takes them up past Edom and Moab toward the country of Sihon (verse 24) and the Jordan.

records.source: וְאֶת־הָעָם֮ צַ֣ו לֵאמֹר֒ אַתֶּ֣ם עֹֽבְרִ֗ים בִּגְבוּל֙ אֲחֵיכֶ֣ם בְּנֵי־עֵשָׂ֔ו הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּשֵׂעִ֑יר וְיִֽירְא֣וּ מִכֶּ֔ם וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And the people command, saying, You [are] passing in [the] territory of your brothers, [the] sons of Esau, who dwell in Seir; and they will be afraid of you, and you will take heed very much.
pieces: And tell the people: "You are going to cross the land of your relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will fear you, and you must take great care.

L.4: And command the people, saying, "You [are] about to pass through the territory of your brothers the sons of Esau, who live in Seir; and they will be afraid of you, and you must take great care.

R.4: Give the people this command: "You are going to travel through the land that belongs to your relatives, the descendants of Esau. They live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.

decisions.choice: your brothers the sons of Esau: the Edomites, a people related to Israel
decisions.reason: Esau was the twin brother of Jacob, who is Israel (Genesis 25:24-26), and his descendants lived in Seir (Genesis 36:8-9). Israel and Edom are "brothers" as nations (Numbers 20:14; Deuteronomy 23:8), and that kinship is part of the reason Israel must not fight them.

decisions.choice: they will be afraid of you, and you must take great care: Edom's fear is no excuse for Israel to take advantage
decisions.reason: The two clauses belong together: because Edom will be afraid, Israel must be all the more careful not to start a fight. Verse 5 says what that care means.

decisions.choice: the message to the people runs from here to the end of verse 7
decisions.reason: God gives Moses words to pass on to the people. Verses 5-7 carry on the same message: what Israel must and must not do in Edom, and why.

decisions.choice: pass through the territory: compare Numbers 20:14-21
decisions.reason: In Numbers 20 the king of Edom refused to let Israel cross his land, and Israel went around it (Numbers 21:4). Here the emphasis is on how Israel was to behave as it went by Edom's people, buying what it needed (verse 6). The route probably ran along Edom's edge rather than through its heartland.

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "brothers", meaning a related people. Balanced and Readable say "relatives" so that the reader does not think of Esau's own brothers; Literal keeps "brothers".

records.source: אַל־תִּתְגָּר֣וּ בָ֔ם כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֤ן לָכֶם֙ מֵֽאַרְצָ֔ם עַ֖ד מִדְרַ֣ךְ כַּף־רָ֑גֶל כִּֽי־יְרֻשָּׁ֣ה לְעֵשָׂ֔ו נָתַ֖תִּי אֶת־הַ֥ר שֵׂעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: Do not engage in strife with them, for not I will give to you of their land even [the] treading of [the] sole of a foot, for [as] a possession to Esau I have given the hill country of Seir.
pieces: Do not start a fight with them, because I will not give you any of their land, not even room enough to set your foot on. I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau as his possession.

L.5: Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even the treading of the sole of a foot, for I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau [as] a possession.

R.5: Do not try to fight them. I will not give you any of their land, not even a footprint's worth. I have given the hills of Seir to Esau's family to be their own.

decisions.choice: provoke: stir up a quarrel or a war
decisions.reason: The verb means to stir oneself up against someone, to start hostilities. It is used again for Moab (verse 9) and Ammon (verse 19), and then, turned round, in God's command to fight Sihon (verse 24).

decisions.choice: the treading of the sole of a foot: the smallest piece of ground
decisions.reason: The space a foot covers when it steps is the least amount of land one could own. Israel is to take nothing at all from Edom.

decisions.choice: I have given ... as a possession: God gives lands to other peoples too
decisions.reason: The word "possession" is the one used for Israel's own land. God has given Seir to Esau, Moab to Lot's descendants (verse 9) and Ammon's land to them as well (verse 19). The asides in verses 10-12 and 20-23 add that other peoples, too, received their lands by God's hand.

decisions.choice: Esau's family
decisions.reason: "Esau" stands for his descendants, the people of Edom. Readable says so.

records.source: אֹ֣כֶל תִּשְׁבְּר֧וּ מֵֽאִתָּ֛ם בַּכֶּ֖סֶף וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֑ם וְגַם־מַ֜יִם תִּכְר֧וּ מֵאִתָּ֛ם בַּכֶּ֖סֶף וּשְׁתִיתֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Food you will buy from them for silver, and you will eat; and also water you will buy from them for silver, and you will drink.
pieces: You are to buy food from them with money so that you can eat, and you are to pay them money for water to drink as well.

L.6: Food you shall buy from them for silver, and you shall eat; and also water you shall buy from them for silver, and you shall drink.

R.6: Pay them money for the food you eat. Pay them for the water you drink too.

decisions.choice: you shall buy ... you shall buy: two different verbs with the same sense here
decisions.reason: The first verb is used for buying grain (Genesis 42:2-3); the second means to make a purchase or bargain (Hosea 3:2). The same second verb can also mean "dig", but "from them for silver" shows that buying is meant.

decisions.choice: silver: money
decisions.reason: There were no coins yet. Payment was made in weighed pieces of silver, so "silver" is the ordinary word for money.

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "money", which is what the silver was used as; Literal keeps "silver".

records.source: כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ בֵּֽרַכְךָ֗ בְּכֹל֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדֶ֔ךָ יָדַ֣ע לֶכְתְּךָ֔ אֶת־הַמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַגָּדֹ֖ל הַזֶּ֑ה זֶ֣ה׀אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֥א חָסַ֖רְתָּ דָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: For Yahweh your God has blessed you in all [the] work of your hand; he has known your walking [through] the wilderness the great this; this forty year[s] Yahweh your God [has been] with you; not you have lacked a thing.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed all that your hands have done. He has cared for you as you made your way through this great wilderness. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has been with you for these forty years, and you have never gone without anything."'

L.7: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you in all the work of your hand; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has known your walking [through] this great wilderness. These forty years {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [has been] with you; you have not lacked a thing."'

R.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed everything you have done. He has taken care of you on your long trip through this huge desert. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has been with you all these forty years, and you have always had what you needed."'

decisions.choice: for: the reason Israel can pay its way
decisions.reason: The blessing God has given explains why Israel can buy food and water instead of taking them (verse 6): the people have the means to pay, and God has never let them go without.

decisions.choice: he has known your walking: he has watched over and cared for your journey
decisions.reason: To "know" here is to take notice of and care for, as in Psalm 1:6, "the LORD knows the way of the righteous".

decisions.choice: your, you: singular here, where verses 4-6 are plural
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy often moves between "you" plural and "you" singular. The singular speaks to Israel as one people; the meaning does not change.

decisions.choice: these forty years: the whole time since the exodus
decisions.reason: Forty years is the span of the wilderness journey (Numbers 14:33-34); verse 14 counts thirty-eight of them from Kadesh-barnea.

decisions.choice: has cared for you as you made your way / has watched over you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "has known your walking", which in English would sound like mere information.

records.source: וַֽנַּעֲבֹ֞ר מֵאֵ֧ת אַחֵ֣ינוּ בְנֵי־עֵשָׂ֗ו הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּשֵׂעִ֔יר מִדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ הָֽעֲרָבָ֔ה מֵאֵילַ֖ת וּמֵעֶצְיֹ֣ן גָּ֑בֶרסוַנֵּ֨פֶן֙ וַֽנַּעֲבֹ֔ר דֶּ֖רֶךְ מִדְבַּ֥ר מוֹאָֽב׃
records.gloss: And we passed on from with our brothers, [the] sons of Esau, who dwell in Seir, from [the] way of the Arabah, from Elath and from Ezion-geber; and we turned and passed on [by the] way of [the] wilderness of Moab.
pieces: So we moved on past our relatives, the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, leaving the road through the Arabah that comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and went along the road through the wilderness of Moab.

L.8: And we passed on away from our brothers the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, away from the way of the Arabah, from Elath and from Ezion-geber. And we turned and passed on [by] the way of the wilderness of Moab.

R.8: So we kept going and left our relatives, Esau's descendants, behind in Seir. We left the road through the Arabah valley that comes up from the towns of Elath and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and took the road through the desert of Moab.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, Elath, Ezion-geber: the rift valley south of the Dead Sea and the towns at its southern end
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the dry valley that runs from the Dead Sea down to the gulf east of Sinai. Elath and Ezion-geber stood at the head of that gulf (1 Kings 9:26).

decisions.choice: away from ... away from the way of the Arabah: Israel left both Edom and the Arabah road behind
alternatives: passed by Edom by way of the Arabah road
decisions.reason: The same word "from" is repeated: Israel moved away from Edom's people and away from the road through the Arabah. The verse can also be read as saying that Israel went past Edom by way of that road. Either way, Israel then turned north-east toward Moab without taking any of Edom's land.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Moab: the open country on Moab's eastern edge
decisions.reason: Israel kept to the steppe east of Moab's farmland and towns, as Numbers 21:11 also says.

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

decisions.choice: the Arabah valley, the towns of
decisions.reason: Readable adds "valley" and "the towns of" so that the reader knows what kind of places these names are.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֶל־תָּ֨צַר֙אֶת־מוֹאָ֔ב וְאַל־תִּתְגָּ֥ר בָּ֖ם מִלְחָמָ֑ה כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֨ן לְךָ֤ מֵֽאַרְצוֹ֙ יְרֻשָּׁ֔ה כִּ֣י לִבְנֵי־ל֔וֹט נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־עָ֖ר יְרֻשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, Do not harass Moab, and do not engage in strife with them [in] battle, for not I will give to you of his land [as] a possession, for to [the] sons of Lot I have given Ar [as] a possession.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not treat Moab as an enemy or start a war with them. I will not give you any of their land to possess, because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their own.'

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not harass Moab, and do not provoke them to battle, for I will not give you any of his land [as] a possession, for to the sons of Lot I have given Ar [as] a possession.'

R.9: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told me, 'Do not attack the Moabites or start a war with them. I will not give you any of their land. I have given Ar to Lot's descendants to be their own.'

decisions.choice: the sons of Lot: Moab and Ammon, descended from Abraham's nephew Lot
decisions.reason: Genesis 19:36-38 traces Moab and Ammon to Lot's two sons. Like Edom, they are relatives of Israel, and God protects their lands for that reason (verse 19).

decisions.choice: harass: treat as an enemy, press hard
decisions.reason: The verb means to be hostile to someone, to besiege or hem them in. Israel is not to act as Moab's enemy at all.

decisions.choice: Ar: a chief town of Moab, standing for Moab's land
decisions.reason: Ar lay near the Arnon, Moab's northern border (Numbers 21:15, 28). Here, as in verses 18 and 29, it stands for Moab's country as a whole.

decisions.choice: his land: Moab spoken of as one person
decisions.reason: Hebrew can speak of a nation as "he". "His land" is the land of Moab, and "them" earlier in the verse is its people.

decisions.choice: their land
decisions.reason: English does not usually call a nation "he"; Balanced and Readable say "their land", and Readable names the Moabites.

records.source: הָאֵמִ֥ים לְפָנִ֖ים יָ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֑הּ עַ֣ם גָּד֥וֹל וְרַ֛ב וָרָ֖ם כָּעֲנָקִֽים׃
records.gloss: The Emim formerly dwelt in it, a people great and numerous and tall like the Anakim.
pieces: (In earlier times the Emim lived there, a great people, numerous and as tall as the Anakim.

L.10: (The Emim formerly lived in it, a people great and many and tall like the Anakim.

R.10: (Long ago a people called the Emim lived in that land. They were a powerful nation with many people, and they were as tall as the Anakim.

decisions.choice: verses 10-12 are an explanatory aside about the peoples who held these lands before
decisions.reason: The LORD's words to Moses stop at the end of verse 9 and take up again in verse 13 ("Now get up and cross ..."). In between stands a note, in the style of a historian, about who lived in Moab and Seir before Moab and Edom. It shows that God had already given lands to Lot's and Esau's descendants by removing peoples as strong as the Anakim, whom Israel had been afraid of (1:28). It is still part of the book's account of Moses' speech, which continues.

decisions.choice: the Emim: the Moabites' name for the earlier people of their land
decisions.reason: Verse 11 says the name was the one the Moabites used. It may mean "the frightening ones"; the Emim are also named in Genesis 14:5. Nothing else is known of them.

decisions.choice: the Anakim: a people famous for their height
decisions.reason: The spies had seen the Anakim in Canaan and called them giants (Numbers 13:22, 28, 33), and fear of them was one reason Israel refused to enter the land (1:28).

decisions.choice: parentheses around verses 10-12
decisions.reason: Parentheses show the reader that these verses are a note set into the LORD's words, not words spoken to Moses. The names Emim and Anakim keep the Hebrew plural ending, as the source data spells them.

records.source: רְפָאִ֛ים יֵחָשְׁב֥וּ אַף־הֵ֖ם כָּעֲנָקִ֑ים וְהַמֹּ֣אָבִ֔ים יִקְרְא֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם אֵמִֽים׃
records.gloss: Rephaim were regarded also they like the Anakim, and the Moabites call them Emim.
pieces: They were reckoned as Rephaim, as the Anakim were, though the Moabites' name for them is Emim.

L.11: Rephaim they also were counted, like the Anakim, and the Moabites call them Emim.

R.11: People thought of them as Rephaim, just like the Anakim. But the Moabites called them Emim.

decisions.choice: Rephaim: a general name for the tall ancient peoples of the region
decisions.reason: The Rephaim appear in Genesis 14:5 and 15:20, and Og king of Bashan was the last of them (3:11). Each people that took over their land had its own name for them: Emim in Moab, Zamzummim in Ammon (verse 20).

decisions.choice: call: the name in use among the Moabites
decisions.reason: The verb form describes what the Moabites customarily called them, and can be read as present ("call") or past ("used to call").

records.source: וּבְשֵׂעִ֞יר יָשְׁב֣וּ הַחֹרִים֮ לְפָנִים֒ וּבְנֵ֧י עֵשָׂ֣ו יִֽירָשׁ֗וּם וַיַּשְׁמִידוּם֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ תַּחְתָּ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר עָשָׂ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְאֶ֨רֶץ֙ יְרֻשָּׁת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And in Seir dwelt the Horites formerly, and [the] sons of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them and dwelt in their place, as did Israel to [the] land of his possession which gave Yahweh to them.
pieces: Seir, too, was once the home of the Horites. The descendants of Esau took it from them, wiping them out as they advanced and settling in their place, just as Israel did in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave it to possess.)

L.12: And in Seir the Horites formerly lived, but the sons of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them and lived in their place, as Israel did to the land of its possession, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave to them.)

R.12: The Horites used to live in Seir. But Esau's descendants forced them out and wiped them out, and then they settled where the Horites had lived. This is just what Israel did in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them to be their own.)

decisions.choice: the Horites: the earlier people of Seir
decisions.reason: Genesis 14:6 names the Horites in their hill country of Seir, and Genesis 36:20-30 lists their clans before Edom's.

decisions.choice: dispossessed: drove them out and took over their land
decisions.reason: The verb used here is the one used for Israel taking possession of its land, and for driving out the nations in it. It joins the two halves of the verse: Edom did to the Horites what Israel did in its own land.

decisions.choice: from before them: as they advanced
decisions.reason: "From before them" means in front of the descendants of Esau, as they moved in.

decisions.choice: as Israel did: the note looks back from a later time
alternatives: the land east of the Jordan, taken in 2:31-3:17
the whole land, after the conquest
decisions.reason: The aside speaks of Israel's taking of its land as already done. It may have in view the land east of the Jordan, which Israel took in this chapter and the next (2:31-3:17) and which was given to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh (3:12-20); or it may look back on the whole land, written from a time after Israel had settled there.

decisions.choice: which the LORD gave to them: the land is God's gift
decisions.reason: Even in a note about other peoples, Israel's land is the land the LORD gave, as Seir was given to Esau (verse 5).

decisions.choice: took it from them / forced them out
decisions.reason: "Dispossess" is the Literal word; Balanced and Readable say what it means for a people. Balanced also speaks of Israel as "it", a nation, where the Hebrew has "its possession" and "to them".

records.source: עַתָּ֗ה קֻ֛מוּ וְעִבְר֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־נַ֣חַל זָ֑רֶד וַֽנַּעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־נַ֥חַל זָֽרֶד׃
records.gloss: Now arise and pass over the wadi of Zered. And we passed over the wadi of Zered.
pieces: 'Rise now and cross over the Zered Valley.' So we crossed over the Zered Valley.

L.13: 'Now arise and cross over the wadi of Zered.' And we crossed over the wadi of Zered.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, 'Now get going and cross the Zered Valley.' So we crossed it.

decisions.choice: the LORD's words from verse 9 take up again here
decisions.reason: After the aside of verses 10-12, the command goes on from where verse 9 stopped. The speaker is the LORD.

decisions.choice: the wadi of Zered: the stream valley on Moab's southern border
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley that carries water in the rainy season and is often dry the rest of the year. The Zered lay between Edom and Moab (Numbers 21:12). Crossing it marked the end of the wilderness years (verse 14).

decisions.choice: The LORD said
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, since the aside has come between the start of the LORD's words and this command.

decisions.choice: the Zered Valley
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:12: Literal says "wadi"; Balanced and Readable use a common English word.

records.source: וְהַיָּמִ֞ים אֲשֶׁר־הָלַ֣כְנוּ׀מִקָּדֵ֣שׁ בַּרְנֵ֗עַ עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־עָבַ֨רְנוּ֙ אֶת־נַ֣חַל זֶ֔רֶד שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנֶ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה עַד־תֹּ֨ם כָּל־הַדּ֜וֹר אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ מִקֶּ֣רֶב הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר נִשְׁבַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And the days which we walked from Kadesh-barnea until that we passed over the wadi of Zered [were] thirty and eight year[s], until was finished all the generation, the men of the war, from [the] midst of the camp, as had sworn Yahweh to them.
pieces: The time from when we left Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley was thirty-eight years. That was how long it took for the whole generation of fighting men to die out from the camp, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had sworn to them.

L.14: And the days that we walked from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed over the wadi of Zered [were] thirty-eight years, until the whole generation, the men of war, had come to an end from the midst of the camp, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had sworn to them.

R.14: From the time we left Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley, thirty-eight years went by. In that time all the men who had been old enough to fight died, and none of them were left in the camp. This happened just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had sworn to them it would.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had sworn to them: the oath that this generation would not enter the land
decisions.reason: When the people refused to go up from Kadesh-barnea, the LORD swore that none of that evil generation would see the good land (1:34-35; Numbers 14:21-35). These verses record that the oath was carried out.

decisions.choice: thirty-eight years: the time from Kadesh-barnea to the Zered
decisions.reason: With the journey from Egypt to Kadesh-barnea, this makes up the forty years of verse 7 and Numbers 14:33-34.

decisions.choice: the men of war: the men counted for the army
decisions.reason: These are the men twenty years old and up who were counted in the census (Numbers 1:3) and who were condemned to die in the wilderness (Numbers 14:29).

decisions.choice: all the men who had been old enough to fight
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the men of war" from Numbers 14:29, so that the reader does not take it to mean only professional soldiers.

records.source: וְגַ֤ם יַד־יְהוָה֙ הָ֣יְתָה בָּ֔ם לְהֻמָּ֖ם מִקֶּ֣רֶב הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה עַ֖ד תֻּמָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And also [the] hand of Yahweh was against them, to throw them into confusion from [the] midst of the camp, until they were finished.
pieces: Indeed, the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against them, sweeping them out of the camp until none of them were left.

L.15: And also the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against them, to rout them from the midst of the camp, until they were finished.

R.15: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} was against them. He kept removing them from the camp until they were all gone.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was against them: God's power at work in judgment
decisions.reason: The "hand" of the LORD is his power. Against someone, it brings punishment (Exodus 9:3; 1 Samuel 5:6).

decisions.choice: rout: throw into confusion and destroy
decisions.reason: The verb is used for God throwing enemy armies into panic in battle (Exodus 14:24; Joshua 10:10). Here it is turned against the rebel generation within Israel's own camp.

decisions.choice: and also: their deaths were not only the passing of time
decisions.reason: Verse 14 says the generation came to an end; this verse adds that it was God's doing, as he had sworn.

decisions.choice: The LORD himself was against them
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the hand of the LORD" in plain words.

decisions.choice: when ... had finished dying: the sentence goes on into verse 17

decisions.choice: a sentence of its own
decisions.reason: Readable ends the sentence here and starts verse 17 with "Then".

decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: אַתָּ֨ה עֹבֵ֥ר הַיּ֛וֹם אֶת־גְּב֥וּל מוֹאָ֖ב אֶת־עָֽר׃

decisions.choice: the border of Moab, Ar: Ar names the place where Israel passes Moab's border
alternatives: the border of Moab, that is, the territory of Ar
decisions.reason: Ar stands beside "the border of Moab" without a linking word. It probably marks the point on Moab's northern edge, by the Arnon, where Israel would pass (Numbers 21:15). It could also stand for the territory of Moab as a whole, as in verses 9 and 29.

decisions.choice: you are crossing today: about to happen now
decisions.reason: The participle describes something on the point of happening. "You" is singular, Israel as one people.

records.gloss: And you will draw near opposite [the] sons of Ammon; do not harass them and do not engage in strife with them, for not I will give of [the] land of [the] sons of Ammon to you [as] a possession, for to [the] sons of Lot I have given it [as] a possession.
pieces: When you come close to the Ammonites, do not treat them as enemies or start a fight with them, for I will not give you any of the Ammonites' land to possess. I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their own.'

L.19: And you will come near opposite the sons of Ammon. Do not harass them and do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of the land of the sons of Ammon [as] a possession, for to the sons of Lot I have given it [as] a possession.'

R.19: You will come near the land of the Ammonites. Do not attack them or try to fight them. I will not give you any of their land, because I have given it to Lot's descendants to be their own.'

decisions.choice: the same command as for Edom and Moab
decisions.reason: The words repeat verses 5 and 9. Edom, Moab and Ammon, Israel's three related neighbors, are each protected by God's gift of their land.

decisions.choice: the sons of Ammon: the Ammonites, east of the upper Jabbok
decisions.reason: Ammon descended from Lot's younger son (Genesis 19:38). Their land lay on the desert side of Sihon's kingdom, around the upper Jabbok (verse 37; Numbers 21:24).

decisions.choice: the Ammonites
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:24: Balanced and Readable name the people; Literal keeps "the sons of Ammon".

records.gloss: [A] land of Rephaim it was regarded, also it; Rephaim dwelt in it formerly, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
pieces: (That land too was counted as a land of the Rephaim. The Rephaim used to live there, though the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,

L.20: (A land of Rephaim it also was counted; Rephaim formerly lived in it, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,

R.20: (This land was also thought of as a land of the Rephaim. Rephaim had lived there long ago. The Ammonites called them Zamzummim.

decisions.choice: verses 20-23 are a second explanatory aside about earlier peoples
decisions.reason: As in verses 10-12, the LORD's words stop (at the end of verse 19) and a note explains who held Ammon's land before the Ammonites, adding the examples of Seir and of the coast near Gaza. The LORD's words take up again in verse 24. The note makes the same point as the first: God gives lands to peoples and takes them away, even from peoples as strong as the Anakim.

decisions.choice: Zamzummim: the Ammonites' name for the Rephaim of their land
decisions.reason: The name is found only here. It may be the same people as the Zuzim of Genesis 14:5, who are named beside the Rephaim and the Emim. Its meaning is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: Rephaim: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: The general name for the tall ancient peoples of the region.

decisions.choice: parentheses around verses 20-23
decisions.reason: As in verses 10-12, the parentheses mark the note set into the LORD's words.

records.source: עַ֣ם גָּד֥וֹל וְרַ֛ב וָרָ֖ם כָּעֲנָקִ֑ים וַיַּשְׁמִידֵ֤ם יְהוָה֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּירָשֻׁ֖ם וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: a people great and numerous and tall like the Anakim; and destroyed them Yahweh from before them, and they dispossessed them and dwelt in their place,
pieces: a great people, numerous and as tall as the Anakim. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} wiped them out to make way for the Ammonites, who took over their land and settled there in their place,

L.21: a people great and many and tall like the Anakim; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed them from before them, and they dispossessed them and lived in their place,

R.21: They were a powerful nation with many people, as tall as the Anakim. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed them as the Ammonites came in. The Ammonites forced them out and settled where they had lived.

decisions.choice: the LORD destroyed them: God rules the history of other nations too
decisions.reason: In verse 12 the descendants of Esau are said to destroy the Horites; here and in verse 22 the LORD is the one who did it. The movement of peoples is God's work, for nations other than Israel as well (Amos 9:7).

decisions.choice: from before them ... they dispossessed them: the Ammonites drove out the Zamzummim
decisions.reason: "Them" after "destroyed" is the Zamzummim; "before them" and "they" are the Ammonites, who then lived in their place.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Ammonites so that the reader can tell the two peoples apart.

pieces: just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done for the descendants of Esau who live in Seir, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wiped out the Horites before them, so that they took over the Horites' land and live there still, to this day.

L.22: just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done for the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroyed the Horites from before them, and they dispossessed them and have lived in their place until this day.

R.22: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} did this for Esau's descendants in Seir too. He destroyed the Horites as Esau's descendants came in. They forced the Horites out, and they still live there today.

decisions.choice: the Horites: as in verse 12
decisions.reason: Verse 12 told how Esau's descendants took Seir from the Horites. Here the same event is credited to God.

decisions.choice: until this day: up to the time of the speaker
decisions.reason: The phrase looks at the situation as it still stood when these words were spoken or written: Edom still held Seir.

decisions.choice: The LORD had done
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and names the LORD, who is the subject of "he did" in the Hebrew (verse 21).

records.source: וְהָֽעַוִּ֛ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֥ים בַּחֲצֵרִ֖ים עַד־עַזָּ֑ה כַּפְתֹּרִים֙ הַיֹּצְאִ֣ים מִכַּפְתּ֔וֹר הִשְׁמִידֻ֖ם וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ תַחְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And the Avvites who dwelt in villages as far as Gaza, [the] Caphtorim who came out from Caphtor destroyed them and dwelt in their place.
pieces: The Avvites, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were wiped out by the Caphtorim, who came from Caphtor and settled where the Avvites had been.)

L.23: And the Avvites, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim who came out from Caphtor destroyed them and lived in their place.)

R.23: Also, the Avvites once lived in villages all the way to Gaza. But the Caphtorim, who came from a land called Caphtor, destroyed them and settled in their land.)

decisions.choice: the Avvites near Gaza: an early people of the coastal plain
decisions.reason: The Avvites lived in the south-west, on the coast near Gaza. Joshua 13:3 still mentions them there.

decisions.choice: the Caphtorim from Caphtor: newcomers from across the sea, linked with the Philistines
decisions.reason: Caphtor is most likely the island of Crete. The Philistines are said to have come from Caphtor (Jeremiah 47:4; Amos 9:7), and Genesis 10:14 names the Caphtorim beside them.

decisions.choice: the last example of the aside: a people that came from far away
decisions.reason: Unlike the earlier examples, this one is not about Israel's relatives, and God is not named. It shows simply that lands change hands. After it, the LORD's words resume in verse 24.

decisions.choice: a land called Caphtor
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Caphtor is a place, without settling where it was.

records.source: ק֣וּמוּ סְּע֗וּ וְעִבְרוּ֮ אֶת־נַ֣חַל אַרְנֹן֒ רְאֵ֣ה נָתַ֣תִּי בְ֠יָדְךָ אֶת־סִיחֹ֨ן מֶֽלֶךְ־חֶשְׁבּ֧וֹן הָֽאֱמֹרִ֛י וְאֶת־אַרְצ֖וֹ הָחֵ֣ל רָ֑שׁ וְהִתְגָּ֥ר בּ֖וֹ מִלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Arise, set out, and pass over the wadi of Arnon; see, I have given into your hand Sihon, king of Heshbon, the Amorite, and his land; begin, take possession, and engage in strife with him [in] battle.
pieces: 'Get up, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. Look, I have handed Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, over to you, and his land with him. Start taking his land, and make war on him.

L.24: 'Arise, set out, and cross over the wadi of Arnon. See, I have given into your hand Sihon king of Heshbon, the Amorite, and his land. Begin, take possession, and provoke him to battle.

R.24: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, 'Get moving now, and cross the Arnon River. Look, I have put Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon, in your power, and his land too. Start taking it over. Go to war against him.

decisions.choice: the LORD's words from verse 19 take up again here
decisions.reason: After the second aside (verses 20-23), the LORD goes on speaking. He now gives the order that ends the time of passing by: cross the Arnon and fight.

decisions.choice: I have given: as good as done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act, though the battle is still to come (verses 32-33). What God has decided is spoken of as already done.

decisions.choice: engage him in battle: the verb Israel was forbidden to use against Edom, Moab and Ammon
decisions.reason: "Do not provoke them" was the command for Israel's relatives (verses 5, 9, 19). With Sihon the same verb becomes a command.

decisions.choice: Sihon king of Heshbon, the Amorite: the ruler of the land north of the Arnon
decisions.reason: Sihon had taken this land from Moab and made Heshbon his capital (Numbers 21:26). The Arnon was Moab's northern border (Numbers 21:13).

decisions.choice: The LORD said
decisions.reason: As in verse 13: Readable names the speaker after the aside.

decisions.choice: the Arnon Valley / the Arnon River
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "wadi". Balanced calls it a valley, as with the Zered (verse 13); Readable calls it a river, as Numbers 21:13 does at that level.

pieces: Starting today I will make the peoples everywhere under heaven dread you and fear you. When they hear reports about you, they will tremble and shake with terror because of you.'

L.25: This day I will begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you on the face of the peoples under the whole heaven, who will hear the report of you and will tremble and writhe because of you.'

R.25: Starting today, I will make nations all over the world afraid of you. When they hear about you, they will shake and be terrified.'

decisions.choice: under the whole heaven: everywhere
decisions.reason: The phrase means the peoples of the world in general. In practice it means those who hear what Israel has done, as the Song at the Sea says of Philistia, Edom, Moab and Canaan (Exodus 15:14-16; compare Joshua 2:9-11).

decisions.choice: be in anguish: writhe with fear
decisions.reason: The verb is used for writhing in pain, as a woman in labor does. Here it is the shaking of deep fear.

decisions.choice: I will begin: God starts now what Israel is to begin in verse 24
decisions.reason: "Begin" is repeated: Israel is to begin to take the land, and God begins to spread fear of Israel before it. Verse 31 uses the word again.

decisions.choice: all over the world
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of "under the whole heaven".

records.source: וָאֶשְׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכִים֙ מִמִּדְבַּ֣ר קְדֵמ֔וֹת אֶל־סִיח֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן דִּבְרֵ֥י שָׁל֖וֹם לֵאמֹֽר׃

R.26: Then I sent messengers from the desert of Kedemoth to Sihon, the king of Heshbon. I offered him peace with this message:

decisions.choice: words of peace: an offer made before any fighting
decisions.reason: God had already said that Sihon was given into Israel's hand (verse 24), yet Moses first asked for peaceful passage. Later law tells Israel to offer peace to a town before attacking it (20:10). Sihon's refusal (verse 30) is what brings on the war.

decisions.choice: Kedemoth: a place on the eastern edge of Sihon's land
decisions.reason: The name means "eastern places". It later became a town of Reuben given to the Levites (Joshua 13:18; 21:37). Its exact site is not known.

decisions.choice: I sent: Moses as leader of Israel
decisions.reason: Numbers 21:21 says that Israel sent the messengers. Here Moses speaks as the one who sent them on the people's behalf.

decisions.choice: an offer of peace / offered him peace
decisions.reason: "Words of peace" are a message proposing peace; Balanced and Readable say so.

R.27: 'Let us go through your land. We will keep to the main road and not leave it to go right or left.

decisions.choice: on the road, on the road: only on the road
decisions.reason: Saying the phrase twice makes it emphatic: Israel will keep to the road and nowhere else, without straying into fields or towns.

decisions.choice: let me pass, I will go: Moses speaks for the whole people

decisions.choice: us, we
decisions.reason: Readable uses "we", since a whole people is asking to pass. Literal and Balanced keep the singular of the message.

records.source: אֹ֣כֶל בַּכֶּ֤סֶף תַּשְׁבִּרֵ֨נִי֙ וְאָכַ֔לְתִּי וּמַ֛יִם בַּכֶּ֥סֶף תִּתֶּן־לִ֖י וְשָׁתִ֑יתִי רַ֖ק אֶעְבְּרָ֥ה בְרַגְלָֽי׃
records.gloss: Food for silver you will sell me, and I will eat; and water for silver you will give to me, and I will drink; only let me pass through on my feet,
pieces: Sell me food for money so that I can eat, and give me water for money so that I can drink. Just let me pass through on foot,

L.28: Food for silver you will sell me, and I will eat; and water for silver you will give me, and I will drink. Only let me pass through on my feet,

R.28: Sell us food and water, and we will pay you for it. Just let us walk through your land.

decisions.choice: let me pass through on my feet: only walking through, taking nothing
decisions.reason: To go through "on foot" means to pass as travelers do, without stopping to take land or goods.

decisions.choice: food for silver, water for silver: the same terms as in Edom
decisions.reason: Moses offers Sihon what God told Israel to do in Edom (verse 6): to pay for everything.

decisions.choice: money / pay
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: us, we
decisions.reason: As in verse 27.

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָֽשׂוּ־לִ֜י בְּנֵ֣י עֵשָׂ֗ו הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּשֵׂעִ֔יר וְהַמּ֣וֹאָבִ֔ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּעָ֑ר עַ֤ד אֲשֶֽׁר־אֶֽעֱבֹר֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן אֶל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: just as did for me [the] sons of Esau who dwell in Seir and the Moabites who dwell in Ar, until that I pass over the Jordan into the land which Yahweh our God [is] giving to us.
pieces: as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is giving us.'

L.29: just as the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, and the Moabites, who live in Ar, did for me, until I cross over the Jordan into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is giving to us.'

R.29: The descendants of Esau in Seir did this for us, and so did the Moabites in Ar. Let us go on until we cross the Jordan River into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God is giving us.'

decisions.choice: as the sons of Esau and the Moabites did for me: they sold Israel food and water
decisions.reason: Numbers 20:18-21 says Edom refused Israel passage through its land, and Deuteronomy 23:5 blames Ammon and Moab for not meeting Israel with bread and water. The comparison here is narrower: as Israel went along their borders, some of their people sold it supplies (verse 6). Exactly how these accounts fit together is not stated.

decisions.choice: until I cross the Jordan: Israel's goal lies west of the river
decisions.reason: Moses tells Sihon that Israel wants only to pass through; the land God is giving is across the Jordan. Sihon's land became Israel's only after he chose to fight (verses 30-36).

decisions.choice: Let us go on
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence here and supplies "Let us go on" to carry the request of verse 28 forward.

records.source: וְלֹ֣א אָבָ֗ה סִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן הַעֲבִרֵ֖נוּ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־הִקְשָׁה֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֶת־רוּח֗וֹ וְאִמֵּץ֙ אֶת־לְבָב֔וֹ לְמַ֛עַן תִּתּ֥וֹ בְיָדְךָ֖ כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: But not was willing Sihon king of Heshbon to let us pass through him, for had hardened Yahweh your God his spirit and had made obstinate his heart, in order to give him into your hand, as [at] the day this.
pieces: But Sihon king of Heshbon refused to let us pass through his land, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart stubborn, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could hand him over to you, as you see today.

L.30: But Sihon king of Heshbon was not willing to let us pass through his [land], for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, in order to give him into your hand, as [it is] this day.

R.30: But Sihon, the king of Heshbon, would not let us go through his land. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God had made him stubborn and unwilling to change. He did this so that you could defeat Sihon, and that is what has happened.

decisions.choice: the LORD had hardened his spirit: Sihon's refusal served God's purpose
decisions.reason: As with Pharaoh (Exodus 4:21; 14:4), the refusal is Sihon's own ("he was not willing"), and God makes it firm so that Sihon's land, which Israel had not asked for, comes into Israel's hands. The two verbs say the same thing twice: "made hard" and "made strong".

decisions.choice: to give him into your hand: to give you victory over him
decisions.reason: "Into the hand" means into the power of someone.

decisions.choice: as this day: as is now the case
decisions.reason: The phrase points to the present situation of Moses' hearers, who now hold Sihon's land (3:12-17).

decisions.choice: your God, your hand: Moses turns to address the people
decisions.reason: In the middle of telling what "we" did, Moses speaks directly to the people ("you", singular) about what God did for them.

decisions.choice: through his [land]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "pass through him", meaning through his territory. Literal supplies "land".

decisions.choice: made him stubborn and unwilling to change
decisions.reason: Readable puts "hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate" in plain words, keeping both halves.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י רְאֵ֗ה הַֽחִלֹּ֨תִי֙ תֵּ֣ת לְפָנֶ֔יךָ אֶת־סִיחֹ֖ן וְאֶת־אַרְצ֑וֹ הָחֵ֣ל רָ֔שׁ לָרֶ֖שֶׁת אֶת־אַרְצֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, See, I have begun to give before you Sihon and his land; begin, take possession, to possess his land.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Look, I have begun to hand Sihon and his land over to you. Start now to take possession, so that his land will be yours.'

L.31: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over before you. Begin, take possession, so as to take possession of his land.'

R.31: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Look, I have started to give you Sihon and his land. Start taking over his land now, so that it will belong to you.'

decisions.choice: I have begun ... begin: God's beginning and Israel's
decisions.reason: The word "begin" from verses 24-25 comes back. God has begun to give, and Israel is to begin to take.

decisions.choice: take possession, so as to possess: an emphatic repetition
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun form are put side by side to stress the point: the land is to become Israel's possession.

records.heading: The defeat of Sihon king of Heshbon

records.source: וַיֵּצֵא֩ סִיחֹ֨ן לִקְרָאתֵ֜נוּ ה֧וּא וְכָל־עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה יָֽהְצָה׃
records.gloss: And came out Sihon to meet us, he and all his people, for the battle, to Jahaz.
pieces: Sihon came out with his whole army to fight us at Jahaz.

L.32: And Sihon came out to meet us, he and all his people, for battle, at Jahaz.

R.32: Then Sihon and his whole army came out to fight us at Jahaz.

decisions.choice: his people: his fighting men
decisions.reason: In a battle report, "all his people" means the men he could bring to war (Numbers 21:23).

decisions.choice: Jahaz: a town north of the Arnon
decisions.reason: Jahaz lay in the land Sihon ruled, on the edge of the wilderness (Numbers 21:23). Its exact site is not known.

decisions.choice: army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "army" for "his people" in this battle setting.

records.source: וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֛הוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ לְפָנֵ֑ינוּ וַנַּ֥ךְ אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֖יו וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And gave him Yahweh our God before us, and we struck him and his sons and all his people.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God handed him over to us, and we defeated him, his sons and all his army.

L.33: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God gave him over before us, and we struck him and his sons and all his people.

R.33: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God let us defeat him. We defeated Sihon, his sons, and his whole army.

decisions.choice: his sons: the reading tradition of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text can be read "his son", one son. The traditional reading that the scribes marked in the margin is "his sons", and the text here follows that. Either way, Sihon's heirs fell with him.

decisions.choice: struck: defeated in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or hit. In war it means to defeat, often with great loss of life.

decisions.choice: the LORD our God gave him over before us: the victory is God's
decisions.reason: Moses says first that God gave Sihon over, and only then that Israel struck him, as God had promised in verses 24 and 31.

decisions.choice: army
decisions.reason: As in verse 32.

records.source: וַנִּלְכֹּ֤ד אֶת־כָּל־עָרָיו֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַֽנַּחֲרֵם֙ אֶת־כָּל־עִ֣יר מְתִ֔ם וְהַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַטָּ֑ף לֹ֥א הִשְׁאַ֖רְנוּ שָׂרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And we captured all his cities at the time that, and we devoted to destruction every city of men, and the women and the little ones; not we left a survivor.
pieces: At that time we captured all his towns and devoted every one of them to destruction, with their men, women and children. We did not leave a single survivor.

L.34: And we captured all his cities at that time, and we devoted to destruction every city of men, and the women and the little ones; we did not leave a survivor.

R.34: At that time we captured all of Sihon's towns. We destroyed every town completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: the men, the women, and the children. No one was left alive.

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction: the towns and their people were given over to God
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for a "devoted thing" in Leviticus 27:28-29: something given up to the LORD for good. In war it means that a town and its people are destroyed and not kept for anyone's gain (Numbers 21:2-3; Deuteronomy 7:2; 20:16-18). Verse 35 shows that here the livestock and goods were kept.

decisions.choice: every city of men: every town with its men
decisions.reason: The word means men, adult males. With "the women and the little ones" it covers the whole population of each town.

decisions.choice: the little ones: children
decisions.reason: The word is used for children too young to fend for themselves, and sometimes for a family's dependents in general.

decisions.choice: destroyed ... completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:2: Readable gives the sense of the term in plain words; Literal and Balanced keep "devote to destruction".

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:2: "cities" in Literal; "towns" in Balanced and Readable, since these were small walled places.

records.source: רַ֥ק הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה בָּזַ֣זְנוּ לָ֑נוּ וּשְׁלַ֥ל הֶעָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָכָֽדְנוּ׃
records.gloss: Only the livestock we plundered for ourselves, and [the] spoil of the cities which we had captured.
pieces: We took only the livestock as plunder for ourselves, along with the spoil from the towns we had captured.

L.35: Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, and the spoil of the cities that we had captured.

R.35: We kept only the animals and the other valuable things we took from the towns.

decisions.choice: only the livestock we took: the ban covered the people, not the animals and goods
decisions.reason: In the war with Sihon, and with Og after him (3:6-7), the people of the towns were destroyed, but Israel kept the animals and plunder. At Jericho, by contrast, everything was devoted to the LORD (Joshua 6:17-19); at Ai the livestock and plunder were again allowed (Joshua 8:2, 27).

decisions.choice: spoil: goods taken from a defeated enemy
decisions.reason: The word covers whatever was carried off after a victory: tools, clothing, metal and other valuables.

decisions.choice: the other valuable things
decisions.reason: Readable explains "spoil" in common words.

records.source: מֵֽעֲרֹעֵ֡ר אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל־שְׂפַת־נַ֨חַל אַרְנֹ֜ן וְהָעִ֨יר אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּנַּ֨חַל֙ וְעַד־הַגִּלְעָ֔ד לֹ֤א הָֽיְתָה֙ קִרְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׂגְבָ֖ה מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אֶת־הַכֹּ֕ל נָתַ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ לְפָנֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: From Aroer which [is] on [the] edge of [the] wadi of Arnon, and the city which [is] in the wadi, and as far as Gilead, not was there a town that was [too] high for us; the all gave Yahweh our God before us.
pieces: From Aroer, which stands at the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the town that lies in the valley, as far as Gilead, not a single town stood too high for us to take. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God gave every one of them over to us.

L.36: From Aroer, which [is] on the edge of the wadi of Arnon, and the city that [is] in the wadi, as far as Gilead, there was not a town that was too high for us; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God gave [them] all over before us.

R.36: We took every town from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon River valley, and the town down in the valley, all the way to Gilead. None of them was too strong for us. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God gave them all to us.

decisions.choice: too high: too strong, out of reach
decisions.reason: A town "too high" is one whose walls and position make it impossible to take. The words answer the fear of 1:28, where the spies reported towns "great and fortified up to heaven".

decisions.choice: from Aroer to Gilead: Sihon's kingdom from south to north
decisions.reason: Aroer stood on the northern rim of the Arnon gorge, Moab's border (Joshua 12:2). Gilead is the hill country to the north, toward the Jabbok.

decisions.choice: the city that is in the wadi: a town in the Arnon valley, not named
decisions.reason: The town is not named here or in Joshua 13:9, 16, which repeats the phrase. It may be Ar or another town down in the valley.

decisions.choice: too high for us to take / too strong for us
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of height and adds "to take" to show what it means; Readable says "too strong"; Literal keeps "too high".

records.source: רַ֛ק אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ בְּנֵי־עַמּ֖וֹן לֹ֣א קָרָ֑בְתָּ כָּל־יַ֞ד נַ֤חַל יַבֹּק֙ וְעָרֵ֣י הָהָ֔ר וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Only to [the] land of [the] sons of Ammon not you drew near, all [the] side of [the] wadi of Jabbok and [the] cities of the hill country, and all that commanded Yahweh our God.
pieces: But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites, the whole region along the Jabbok River and the towns in the hill country, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God had commanded.

L.37: Only to the land of the sons of Ammon you did not come near, all the side of the wadi of Jabbok and the cities of the hill country, and all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God had commanded.

R.37: But you stayed away from the land of the Ammonites. You did not go near the land along the Jabbok River or the towns in the hills. You did just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God had commanded.

decisions.choice: and all that the LORD our God had commanded: Israel kept to the limits God set
alternatives: and every place that the LORD our God had forbidden
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief: "and all that the LORD our God commanded". It most likely means that Israel stayed away from every place the LORD had told it not to go near (verse 19), so that Israel acted as he had commanded. It could also continue the list, "and all the places the LORD had forbidden". Either way, Israel obeyed.

decisions.choice: all the side of the wadi of Jabbok: the land along the upper Jabbok, Ammon's territory
decisions.reason: The upper course of the Jabbok bends round through the land of the Ammonites, whose border Israel did not cross (Numbers 21:24).

decisions.choice: you did not come near: Moses turns to address the people
decisions.reason: As in verse 30, Moses moves from "we" to "you" (singular), the people as one.

decisions.choice: the Jabbok River
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:24 at Readable; Literal keeps "wadi".
